input.quote: The exclusive remedy of either party in a claim against the other under this Agreement shall be the recovery of its direct damages. In no event shall either party be liable to the other for the recovery of any special, indirect or consequential damages
input.rationale: Section 15 is mutual and excludes indirect/consequential damages, and it carves out Sections 13 (IP) and 14 (confidentiality), but it contains no monetary cap at all, so both parties' direct-damages exposure is unlimited — the fallback (mutual cap of 12 months' fees) is not met. We proposed adding the mutual cap (greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000), expanding the carve-outs to indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud, and confirming fees are not "damages".

input.quote: Garman agrees to indemnify Sparkling and hold it harmless from any and all losses, damages and expenses including without limitation, court costs, arbitration fees, penalties, fines, amounts paid in settlement of claims and reasonable legal fees and expenses of investigation (collectively the "Losses") which Sparkling or any of its respective officers or directors may incur due to a breach of this warranty.
input.rationale: Garman warrants title/non-infringement and indemnifies Sparkling for Losses from breach of that warranty, with the usual procure/modify/replace remedies, and Section 15 places Section 13 outside the liability limitation, so the indemnity is effectively uncapped. This sits at or above the fallback. Minor points noted only: the 10-day notice requirement is tight and there is no express refund remedy or indemnity for Garman's breach of law or gross negligence.
